articleTitle: Solana a New Blockchain Revolution for Indian Agri Products Using Cloud Based Wallet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Agriculture is a wide industry in India and the supply chain for the same is very complex. Even though farming, distributing and selling Agri products are quite evolved, still Post-harvest dubiety is the biggest issue faced by the Indian agriculture market. Hence, farmers will be never benefited from fault pricing, improper sorting and grading of farmed products, lack of proper storage facility and middleman hoarding of vegetables to manipulate rates in the market. These issues will take more time for vegetables to reach consumers and hence quality and freshness of these products get compromised. Block chain technology can revolutionize these pertaining challenges in agriculture. It can help to provide quality Agri products from farmer to consumer. This paper examines the Solana blockchain enabled model in Indian farming. Solana provides the fastest blockchain ecosystem and follows Proof Of History which is more secure with less transaction cost. Scalability is the biggest advantage in Solana when compared with any other blockchain technology. Proof of History consensus makes transaction processing using Solana very efficient as the network breaks down data into smaller chunks making it easy to transfer across the network. It is the fastest blockchain in existence today. The framework proposed is to overcome current issues faced by supply chain in Indian agriculture through cost effective manner. Keywords: Block chain, Block chain technology, Solana, Proof of History, Agri products.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sustainable Maintenance Operations Through Intelligent Climbing Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This paper investigates strategies for enhancing the operational effectiveness of climbing robots in performing maintenance tasks in hard-to-reach environments, with a particular emphasis on historical infrastructures like bridges and tunnels. We focus on optimizing the Wall-pushing Autonomous Maintenance Robot (WAuMBot) to rectify issues associated with mechanical sag. Accurate sag compensation is vital for ensuring precise robot localization and motion, especially in challenging spatial contexts such as the steel arches of the Sydney Harbour Bridge. Our research presents a novel methodology that employs sensor fusion and closed -loop control mechanisms for accurate sag error correction. This optimization significantly refines WAuMBot's odometric accuracy, facilitating advanced multi-step planning without necessitating re-Iocalization steps. The augmented capabilities of climbing robots, demonstrated by WAuMBot's enhanced sag correction performance, contribute to the objectives of sustainable maintenance by curtailing deterioration, reducing environmental and social consequences, and offering greater energy and resource efficiency compared to traditional human-operated methods. Moreover, the utility of these robots in high-risk environ-ments substantially increases workplace safety, worker well-being, and overall operational sustainability. The efficacy and viability of the proposed approach have been confirmed through empirical experiments, indicating its promising applications in the maintenance of bridges and analogous infrastructures.

articleTitle: Frugal Design: An Empirical Conceptualization and Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Designers/Engineers must practice Frugal design to address rising cost-conscious consumption. However, It has been observed that the conception of frugal design and its measurement scale have not yet been created. A three-stage mixed-method research approach was used to identify and validate the frugal design measuring attributes. Stage 1 determined initial frugal design attributes using existing literature research, word frequency count analysis, and expert review content analysis. Survey research (n = 250) was undertaken in Stage 2, and a Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was carried out to refine the preliminary attributes. The final stage involved a survey with a sample of (n=500) Brazilians. To validate the final attribute for gauging frugal design, the Delphi consensus method was used). The frugal design scale provides a framework for organizations to assess frugality based on minimizing inequalities amongst diverse income groups and maximizing well-being by delivering efficient solutions for all groups of people.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Semantic Vector Search Model for Grading and Assessing Students
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The introduction of technology-based learning is attracting considerable attention. With its ability to train learners, and assess and grade their academic work, this platform is a critical component of educational teaching and learning. Most importantly, the learning process is dependent on the human cognitive process in terms of how we learn, perceive, think, and interpret information. Therefore, technology-based teaching and learning is a crucial aspect of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology. As AI evolves, researchers are producing innovative works based on AI. However various data search-retrieval mechanisms in instructional teaching models are struggling to comprehend and understand both structured and unstructured data as most data stores are conversant with structured data. The need for unstructured data as a component of decision-making is growing rapidly. In support of this, such data must be available in the appropriate structured format. In this study, we examine models of cognitive performance using semantic vector search on learner's psychology, and how the two relate throughout the learning process. We comparatively evaluated the application of two core artifacts: context similarity and content awareness. By comparative analysis, the result suggests that semantic search with content similarity and awareness in vector databases ensures an adaptive and intelligent search retrieval. This approach is considered the best for grading and assessing academic work while improving intuitive cognitive abilities.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of MP6 Micro Pumps (Piezoelectric Diaphragm) for Remote Automated Water Quality Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This research paper assesses the efficacy of piezo-electric diaphragm pumps in an automated remote sensor system intended for the detection of pollutant concentrations in water bodies. More precisely, this study aims to evaluate the pumps' operational efficiency when subjected to different angles and heights in order to replicate the roll conditions experienced by an unmanned small boat. To replicate the movement of the boat, experiments were conducted within a controlled laboratory setting and involved the use of a stepper-powered apparatus. Various static tests were conducted at different angles, while dynamic tests were performed by rotating the rig in a back-and-forth motion. The results show a slight decrease in the mean flow rate, going from 4.12 ml/min during static testing to 3.52 ml/min during dynamic testing. The findings enhance our understanding of the reliability and effectiveness of the pumps in relation to their intended use.

articleTitle: Opportunities and Challenges in Agri-Food Systems Enabled by Advance in Electronics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Advances in sensors, IoT and semiconductors have steered significant growth in various aspects of our modern world. Food production and security is one of the most important problem humanity is facing currently, and there is an urgent need for innovative solutions for this problem that demands diverse disciplines to come together for effective and timely solution and implementation. In this paper, we identify some of the key technologies in electronics that could potentially transform the current state-of-the-art in precision agriculture and also discuss critical challenges that needs to be overcome in order to fully tap into potential of cutting-edge advances in electronics to drive innovation in sustainable agri-food systems.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Active Suspension System Using MATLAB/Simulink
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a robust control for active suspension systems. An active suspension system offers superior vehicle handling under varying load conditions than a passive suspension system. However, active suspension systems response interaction with road bumps generates higher command signal when not controlled. Thus, the mathematical and physical modelling approaches are shown and compared. The models are distinguished in terms of their dynamic characteristics to determine the size and control of the actuator. The control design objectives are satisfying passenger comfort and improving vehicle handling. A theoretical framework for analysis the system stability and control gain is provided. The simulation results evaluate the improved performance of the robust controller during acceleration, braking, cornering, a bump height, and rough road profile.

articleTitle: Development of MEMS Boiler Tank for Miniature ORC Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This paper proposed a silicon boiler tank for a miniature organic Rankine cycle power generation system. Demand for miniature power generation systems is increasing with the spread of loT (Internet of Things) devices. Energy harvesting technology is attracting attention as a power generation system that can replace conventional batteries, but the amount of power generated is low. Therefore, we focused on the miniaturization of the organic Rankine cycle (ORC), which can utilize low-temperature waste heat and generates power through electromagnetic induction. The target ORC power generation system is a heat cycle that utilizes waste heat below 473 K on a centimeter-scale. The boiler tank to be developed has both boiler and storage functions in the cycle. By using MEMS (Micro Electro Mechanical Systems) technology, a silicon microfabrication technology, the millimeter-scale boiler tank of 8.0 mm, 10 mm, and 4.5 mm in height will be realized. The developed MEMS boiler tank was filled with low-boiling-point material and evaluated through heating and turbine rotation experiments. In the heating experiment, phase change of the internal fluid was confirmed. In addition, it became clear that the relationship between the direction of heating, the flow path, and the location of the storage section was important. In the rotation experiment, the developed MEMS turbine was connected to the boiler tank and observed. The rotational speed of 2631.6 rpm was obtained when the boiler tank was heated at 373K. These results suggest that the silicon boiler tank shows expected as an element of a small ORC power generation system.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of Hybrid Hydrogen Fuel-Cell/PV/Wind Turbine/Battery/Diesel Energy System for Rural Coastal Community in Western Australia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: A Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES) is the most feasible and sustainable method for replacing the current conventional diesel generation system with the aim of decarbonization, as well as providing a continuous and stable power supply to residents in rural areas worldwide. Hydrogen energy storage technology is a promising method for producing clean electricity and reducing C02 emissions compared to solar PV and wind turbine power systems. This study presents the techno-economic analysis of the Fuel cell / PV / Wind / Battery / Diesel HRES in a rural region in Western Australia using HOMER. Three system configurations with different penetration levels of hydrogen generation have been compared in terms of financial costs and decarbonization. The results show that HRES integrated with hydrogen technology has a good performance in reducing C02 emissions. The high penetration of the fuel cell HRES results in a reduction of 653 kg/year. However, costs such as Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) and Net Present Cost (NPC) are still not as price-competitive as HRES without a hydrogen fuel cell. The optimal off-grid design identified in this case study is the scenario involving an optimal Fuel cell/PV/Wind turbine/Diesel/Battery HRES with an NPC of $4.580 million and an LCOE of $0.5238/kWh for energy costs.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Mechanical Recycling Technique to Recover Metal and Glass from Used Solar Photovoltaic Panels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The projection of conversion from non-renewable sources of energy to greener ones is projected to rise in the coming years and decades to combat the rising effect of global warming. One of the most commonly used and dependent source of renewable energy across the world is solar energy which is largely harnessed by polycrystalline photovoltaic panels (PV). As any other material subjected to the harsh environmental conditions of UV, rain and wind, PV panels have an equally limited durability in service which is limited to 25–30 years. The surge in solar farms and increasing use of PV panels in the last decades is prompting for a new approach to look at the recycling of PV panels in order to re-use existing resources and minimize the adverse impact of waste disposal in the environment. In this study, a low-cost mechanical system to dismantle and recycle the frame structure of PV panels is proposed. The study mainly focuses on the design, testing and manufacturing of the recycling equipment. The findings of this study aim to raise the awareness about the recycling of widely used materials and components in PV panels and to drive new approaches at promoting recycling.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Cooling of PV Panel Embedded with PCM, Fins and Water
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Thermal management of photovoltaics (PV) is significant to improve the performance of PV panel. A novel passive cooling techniques with PCM, fins, and water was developed in the previous research work conducted by the authors. The objective of this paper is to numerically simulate the performance of the cooling technique. An attempt to predict the temperature is made with the considered cooling technique. With the numerical analysis aimed for 5 W panel, the model is studied for its validation and applicability to large-scale PV panels. The governing equations are sorted out from the literature review. This research is performed using ANSYS software to simulate the preliminary model. The research outcomes show that the numerical results have a deviation of about 1.6% for uncooled PV and 9% for cooled PV when compared with the experimental results. This deviation is primarily attributed to the unaccounted losses due to wind velocity, water temperature and varying irradiation that occurs while performing the real time experimentation. Which was not considered in the proposed Finite Element Analysis (FEA) modelling.

articleTitle: Energy Management System for a Microgrid with Photovoltaic/Fuel-Cell (PV/FC) Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Microgrids are the future of the electric power system, and for their proper functioning, the energy management system (EMS) must be designed in order to find the best way to meet the loads with reliability. This study aims to simulate an EMS for a system composed of two distributed energy resources: photovoltaic panels and fuel cell. In addition, an battery energy storage system is used, and the state of charge of these batteries is the main responsible in EMS decision-making. The algorithm is implemented in MATLAB® and analyzed in two different scenarios (grid-connected and isolated), generating curves with the power contribution of each source and the battery's state of charge over time. In both cases, the EMS was able to feed load all time, without needing to feeding to feed only priority loads. However, results showed that the energy provided by the photovoltaic system is not enough for a long operation in islanded mode. In that case, the fuel cell have to activated so that the load can be fed.

articleTitle: Predicting Dominance of Toxic-Producing Cyanobacteria Genus by Machine Learning in a Eutrophic River in South Korea
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Climate crisis is aggravating harmful algal blooms globally. Especially, cyanobacteria harmful algal blooms (CBs) produce taste and odorous compounds and cyanotoxins (microcystins), thereby threatens human health and ecosystem. Cyanotoxins are known to be produced by mainly Microcystis, Anabaena, Oscillatoria, and Aphanizomenon, In the Republic of Korea, extreme CBs occur at the Nakdong River every summer. This study examined spatial distribution of cyanobacterial composition, characterizes major environmental factors influencing microcystins by using machine learning models in the Nakdong River. It was shown that only Microcystis was significant for microcystin and higher ratio of nitrogen to phosphorous contributes to lower microcystin.

articleTitle: Novel Approach to Underwater Object Detection Using Sonar Sensors for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Object detection in sonar images is a vital component of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), serving underwater exploration, surveillance, and environmental monitoring applications. Despite the unique challenges posed by sonar data, including noise, limited resolution, and varying acoustic conditions, this paper presents a comparative study of YOLOv8, a state-of-the-art deep learning model optimized for object detection in sonar images. The study outlines the adaptations made to YOLOv8 to enhance its suitability for sonar data, introduces a meticulously curated sonar image dataset, and details data preprocessing techniques. Rigorous experiments evaluate the performance of YOLOv8, considering key metrics like precision, recall, F1-score, and mean average precision (mAP). Our results reveal valuable insights into the suitability of YOLO-based models for sonar image object detection in AUVs. We compare the detection accuracy, speed, and robustness of YOLOv8 in underwater environments. Furthermore, we discuss the practical implications of our findings and highlight potential areas for future research. This research contributes to the advancement of autonomous underwater systems by enhancing their ability to detect and identify objects of interest in challenging sonar imagery. The findings presented in this paper provide valuable guidance for selecting and optimizing deep learning models for real-world underwater applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Timescale Voltage and Reactive Power Control Method Combining Fast PV PCS and Slow Transformer Tap Response Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: In maintaining the power system voltages, one of the major voltage regulators, the tap-changing transformers in a substation, play an important role during relatively slow load changes. In recent years, as a countermeasure against global warming, the introduction of renewable energy such as photovoltaic power generation system (PV) into the power system has progressed rapidly, and along with this, the amount of net load fluctuations has also changed rapidly as most of PV are connected on the customer side. As a result, it is becoming difficult to maintain the system voltages by controlling the low-speed tap change of transformers only. To suppress fast voltage fluctuations caused by PV output fluctuations, a lot of research work on reactive power control using power conditioning system (PCS) of PV is underway. However, it is difficult to coordinate high-speed PCS reactive power control with low-speed tap change of transformers. In this paper, the authors have proposed a multi-timescale control method that can coordinate low-speed tap change of transformers and high-speed PCS power factor (PF) based reactive power control using deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulation using a power system model that considers a large-scale PV interconnection.

articleTitle: Enhanced Single Diode Model for Bifacial PV Module Incorporating Partial Shading
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Bifacial photovoltaic (PV) technology, designed to harness solar energy from both the front and rear surfaces of solar modules, presents a promising avenue for enhancing solar energy capture. While the Single Diode Model (SDM) has been widely validated for monofacial PV modules, its accuracy in the context of bifacial modules remains underexplored. This paper presents an advanced SDM, originally tailored for mono facial solar cells, adapted to accommodate the unique characteristics of bifacial PV modules, including the incorporation of partial shading effects. The paper explores bifacial solar cell technologies, bifacial gain parameters, and the lEC TS 60904-1-2 specification, emphasizing the significance of accurate PV modeling in system simulation. The model's accuracy is validated using manufacturer datasheets, which includes variations in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Isc$</tex> (short-circuit current), <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Voc$</tex> (open-circuit voltage), and Pmax (maximum power output) for different bifacial gains. Additionally, a modeling approach for partial shading is presented and validated using available experimental data from previous research.

articleTitle: Impact of EV Charger on the Utility Grid and Reactive Power Operation of EV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The rapid integration of Electric Vehicles (EV s) poses a significant concern for energy producers, transmitters, and distributors regarding the capability of the existing grid topology and technology. EV owner prefers to use high-rated chargers to reduce the charging time, negatively impacting the grid. This paper focuses on the impact of different power ratings of chargers and the abilities of EV s for reactive power support to the utility grid. This analysis considers two sizes of popular EV chargers to assess their impact on the utility grid. An IEEE 14 bus network is employed in this study to investigate the grid performance with three different levels of EV penetration (small, medium, and high). The simulation results show that the fast chargers can significantly impact the power system, mainly when the EV penetration is very high.

articleTitle: Improving the Flexural Behaviour of Small Clear 3D-Printed PLA Specimens Through Generative Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The interest to look into alternative engineered materials, which would maximize the efficiency and performance attributes in numerous modern engineering application as well as to push the boundary imposed by present-day material science in the field engineering, is ever so high. One commonly searched feature in engineered materials is their high strength-to-weight ratio. The new AI (Artificial Intelligence) -driven technique of generative design has revolutionized the method of design refinement in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) by enabling advanced optimization techniques which was formerly-unavailable. This study seeks to apply the technique of generative design to improve the flexural behaviour of small clear Polylactic acid (PLA) specimens produced through the additive manufacturing process. The results obtained have shown that despite the optimized material geometry and weight, the refined model was still able to bear significantly high bending loads. Further analysis via the Finite Element Method (FEM) was conducted to substantiate the experimental investigation. Findings of this study illustrates the benefits of generative design which can seamlessly provide advanced design refinements all while preserving or enhancing mechanical performance of the material.

articleTitle: Estimation of State for GPS-Denied Navigation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in Underwater Exploration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: During the AUV mission, localization and Navigation are crucial. AUVs use various methods of Navigation, such as Vision- Based Navigation, INS, Doppler Velocity Logs (DVL), and depth sensors to estimate their position and orientation. This information guides the A UV along the planned path and maintains accurate positioning. Before deploying the AUV, a mission plan is created. This plan includes the survey area, waypoints, and mission objectives. The survey area is typically defined based on the desired coverage and specific areas of interest. Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) have gained significant attention in marine exploration and research due to their ability to operate in challenging environments without direct human intervention. However, accurate Navigation of AUVs remains a critical issue, particularly in scenarios where GPS signals are unavailable or unreliable such as underwater missions. This paper presents a novel state estimation method to enable GPS-denied Navigation for AUVs in marine environments. This proposed method combines sensor data, including IMU, Doppler velocity log, and pressure sensors, to accurately estimate the vehicle's position, orientation, and velocity. We employ EKF and UKF framework to perform the state estimation process, which fuses the different sensor measurements and models the system's uncertainties.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control System for Efficient Energy Management in the Oil and Gas Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This article focuses on developing a smart Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HV AC) control system tailored for the oil, gas, and energy industry. We discuss methods for developing an automated sensor monitoring system and regulating sensor parameters for air conditioning and temperature control. The proposed HV AC intelligent system receives real-time data from temperature sensors, leak sensors, air conditioners, and switches. The article presents the system's architecture, its operational principles, structural diagrams of the control unit, as well as the monitoring and control system. The central part of the real-time monitoring and control system was implemented using the SCADA program for regulating and monitoring sensor parameters. This work underscores the potential of intelligent HV AC systems in promoting energy conservation, enhancing operational safety, and catering to the specific needs of the oil and gas sectors.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Endoskeleton-Type Assist Suit “Sustainable” Based on Musculoskeletal Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Nowadays, power assist suits have been widely used in various fields such as agriculture, nursing care, construction and transportation industries. Power assist suits are divided into exoskeleton and endoskeleton. Recently, endoskeleton has attracted an attention due to its user friendliness. However, under wearing the endoskeleton, since the compressive force is directly added to the wearer's spine due to its structure, it may adversely affect the wearer's lumbar disc. Actually, the lumbar burdens while lifting the heavy object under wearing the endoskeleton have not been fully investigated. The purpose of this study is to perform accurate dynamic analysis of the lumbar burdens under wearing the endoskeleton-type assist suit “Sustainable”. Therefore, in this study, a motion of lifting and taking down the harvest as agricultural work, and a motion of transfer work as nursing care, were captured by the motion capture under wearing and not wearing the Sustainable. Then, the lumbar burdens were analyzed by using the musculoskeletal model software “AnyBody Modeling System”. In addition, the results of analysis and the experimental results obtained in our previous study were compared. As a result, validity of the analysis using the AnyBody Modeling System for the captured motions was indicated. Thus, from the results of analysis, usefulness of the Sustainable to reduce the burden on the subject's lower back was confirmed.

articleTitle: Digital Construction: Revolutionizing Electrical Design with BIM and Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: In the contemporary architectural and construction domain, a paradigm shift is evident through the adoption of Building Information Modeling (BIM) and sophisticated project review tools, notably Revit and Navisworks. This paper delves into this transformative journey from conventional 2D drafting methodologies to the intricate realm of 3D modeling, emphasizing its revolutionary impact on electrical design and the broader construction arena. Central to our exploration is a case study on electrical design of commercial aviation project located in California, USA meticulously developed using Revit software. This project serves as a testament to the enhanced precision, collaboration, and holistic insights afforded by these advanced tools, reshaping the trajectory of building design and construction. Through this paper, we aim to elucidate the multifaceted benefits, challenges, and the overarching implications of integrating BIM and associated technologies in modern construction endeavors.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Voltage Source PWM Rectifier for Electric Vehicle Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in the proportion of electrical energy which is coming from renewable sources to reduce greenhouse gas emission. An energy storage system (ESS) associated with these sources are to balance energy production with consumption. when subjected to low DC voltages and large currents, necessitating specialized power converters. Hence, this work formulated a three-phase, voltage source converter which can be used in a single conversion stage to produce a variable DC voltage at the terminals. In this, a modified Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM) technique is incorporated to produce a Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) signals for voltage source rectifier. This topology is suitable for electric vehicle (EV) applications.

articleTitle: Examining the Capability of a Large-Scale Solar PV Plant for Providing Frequency Support Service
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Maintaining power system stability and reliability using traditional techniques is getting outdated with a perpetual increase in renewables and retiring synchronous generators. Disconnecting renewable plants, including solar PV, is still a common practice in case of significant system disturbances. However, in a 100% renewable scenario, these plants must provide continuous voltage and frequency support. With changing system strength conditions, evaluating whether solar plants can provide frequency support in different system strength conditions is essential. This paper examines the capability of large-scale solar PV to provide frequency support in weak, strong, and very strong system strength conditions. A droop mechanism is used to control the solar PV plant in a single-machine infinite bus (SMIB) system under various contingency events like transmission line faults and sudden load increase and decrease to create over and under-frequency events. The system was modelled and simulated in the PSCAD analytical software tool. It is concluded that the large-scale solar PV plant can provide frequency support after all disturbances not only in strong and very strong grid conditions but also in weak grid conditions.

articleTitle: A Voltage and Reactive Power Control Method Based on Sequential Updated Control Targets Considering Machine Learning Enabled Customer Voltage Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This paper focuses on a voltage and reactive power control (VQC) method that is used to control transformer taps and reactive power devices in substations in order to maintain the system voltage. With increasing share of renewable energy sources and lack of voltage regulating devices on multiple lines connecting to substations with transformers, the existing VQC methods are not effective in maintaining the voltage and needs to be improved. To address this issue, the authors have proposed a new VQC method which can sequentially update the control targets in real time while considering the customer voltages estimated by applying the machine learning technique. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation studies carried out on a standard sub-transmission system model in Japan.

articleTitle: Different Droop Control-Based PV-Wind-Hydro Grid-Connected Microgrid Under Different Load Variations and EV Charging Point Using Different Dispatch Technique and Derivative-Free Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This research work presents the comparative study of the performance of constant IQ droop, Constant Q and voltage Q droop controller on a dispatch controlled optimized hybrid grid tied microgrid system having electrical, industrial and EV (electric vehicle) loads. The optimized configuration of the microgrid on top of load following (LF) and cycle charging (CC) dispatch methods have been determined using a propri-etary derivative free algorithm and their voltage, active power, frequency and reactive powers have been evaluated for the three different control strategies. For the planned microgrid, it has been determined through the analysis in the proposed location, the two dispatch strategies offer similar optimization results and constant IQ droop control offers slightly better performance among the others. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the microgrid system with the proposed controller and operating strategy.

articleTitle: Agrivoltaics: Integrating Solar Energy Generation with Livestock Farming in the Canterbury Region of Aotearoa New Zealand
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Agrivoltaics is the integration of agriculture and solar energy production and seeks to find synergies between the two to create a complementary system. With increased interest in energy generation with utility-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in Aotearoa New Zealand, agrivoltaics provides the opportunity to increase the productivity of land, contribute to the generation of renewable energy without displacing food production, and potentially optimize farming and environmental outcomes. Case study analyses were carried out on a dairy farm and a sheep and beef farm, both located in the Canterbury region. These considered both technical designs and financial analyses. The sheep and beef case study analysis indicated a significant opportunity for farmers to increase their profitability by incorporating agrivoltaics into their farming enterprise. This comes at a time of increased interest in complementary revenue streams due to reduced farmgate product prices, increased working expenses, and increased compliance costs and associated administrative workload. The financial analysis of agrivoltaics for the dairy farm case study suggested it was significantly less lucrative and indicates that incorporating solar generation on these farms might be best suited to non-productive areas or the installation of panels on shed roofs, rather than agrivoltaics. The study provides evidence that agrivoltaics is worthy of further consideration, particularly due to the way in which it offers solutions to some of the major challenges of standard utility-scale solar PV generation. It is evident that the significant gaps in literature need to be addressed to further understand what the potential financial, environmental and social impacts are for the people of Aotearoa New Zealand.

articleTitle: A Systematic Assessment of the Challenges Towards Sustainable Urban Transportation: A Case Study of the Island of Mauritius
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The rapid growth of vehicles in Mauritius exhibits many transport-related problems as faced by many other developed and developing countries, such as heavy traffic congestion, road accidents, high fuel consumption and carbon emission. Despite ongoing efforts from the Government, the influx in the city centre and major towns has amplified given the fact that most industries are located in urban regions. Studies conducted for Mauritius are very limited or minimal related to land use planning (L UP) and sustainable transport. The aim of this study is to investigate into the factors contributing to the growth of unsustainable urban transport behaviours in Mauritius. The literature review and subsequent analysis led to the development of a taxonomy of land transport. This was done in order to simplify and understand the distinct dimensions of the transport sector. Moreover, the system dynamic model sheds light on various factors causing the increasing number of vehicles which is the root cause of the transport problem on the island. Furthermore, this contributed largely to identify the most appropriate strategies that can be adopted to eliminate alleviate transport problems in Mauritius. Future research using the Multi-Agent Transport Simulation software can be considered to better understand travel behaviour and travel demands of the population that will help to come with better strategies.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Road Safety: YOLOv8-Powered Driver Fatigue Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Driver fatigue is a significant cause of road accidents. Effective real-time fatigue detection systems are necessary to improve road safety. Utilizing a lightweight and fast model and creating an effective fatigue judgment rule is important in detecting fatigue in real-time. In this research, we propose a fatigue detection model based on You Look Only Once version 8 (YOLOv8) model to detect driver's facial features and use percentage of eyelid closure over the pupil over time (PERCLOS) and Percentage of Open Mouth (POM) indicators to identify fatigue. This research is divided into two parts. The first part involves creating, labeling, and preprocessing the dataset. We use the YawDD dataset as the original dataset and manually label a new dataset using the Roboflow platform. We then preprocessed the new dataset to train the YOLOv8 model for face features detection. In the second part, we established a multi-indicator fatigue determination rule that uses PERCLOS and POM indicators and set a threshold to determine whether the driver is fatigue. By combining the YOLOv8 model with the fatigue determination rules based on PERCLOS and POM, we successfully built a model to identify a driver's fatigue. Finally, the fatigue detection model based on YOLOv8 achieves a high accuracy rate of 96.9% and a high speed of 11.4 ms/frame in face features detection, surpassing other traditional models and previous generations of YOLO models. This model can effectively detect fatigue in both driver-driving pictures and videos.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach to Predicting Melbourne Housing Prices Using Advanced Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This research rigorously explores the intricate correlations between property attributes and housing prices in Melbourne, aiming to refine price prediction accuracy. Positive correlations observed with ‘Rooms,’ ‘Bedroom2,’ ‘Bathroom,’ ‘Landsize,’ and ‘BuildingArea’ underscore the intuitive link between property size and price, while negative associations with ‘Distance,’ ‘Y earBuilt,’ and ‘PropertyCount’ emphasize the influential role of location, age, and market demand. Multiple modeling approaches were employed and compared for their predictive prowess. Among these, the Random Forest model (Approach 5) stands out with an exceptional R-squared value of 0.81, showcasing its adeptness in capturing complex data relationships effectively. Notably, the inclusion of categorical variables and leveraging localized data in conjunction with Random Forest (Approach 6) also yielded an impressive R-squared value of 0.81, underlining the pivotal role of nuanced information in precise predictions. Furthermore, XGBoost (Approach 7) demonstrated commendable performance, achieving an R-squared value of 0.80, showcasing the versatility of boosting techniques. The comparison of these approaches emphasizes the significance of methodical analysis and model selection in predicting housing prices accurately. The findings underscore the superiority of ensemble methods, especially Random Forest, and the importance of incorporating categorical and localized information for precise price estimations in Melbourne's dynamic real estate market. This comprehensive investigation highlights the exceptional performance of Random Forest and underscores the significance of leveraging nuanced data for superior predictive accuracy. Recommendations stemming from this study advocate for the adoption of ensemble methods, specifically Random Forest and XGBoost, while emphasizing the critical role of categorical variables and localized insights for refining housing price predictions in Melbourne. These insights offer a robust roadmap for enhancing predictive accuracy and guiding informed decisions in real estate.

articleTitle: Enhancing Patient Data Security Through Blockchain Adoption in Fiji's Healthcare System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Ensuring the security of patient data is of utmost importance in healthcare systems worldwide, and Fiji is no exception to this concern. With healthcare providers in Fiji gradually transitioning to digital health records and information sharing, the need to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of patient data becomes a top priority. While there is a wealth of literature discussing the utilization of blockchain technology in the healthcare sector, the novelty of this study lies in its focus on developing a blockchain-based information system tailored explicitly for Fiji to bolster the security of patients' data. This research endeavors to explore the potential of blockchain technology in enhancing the security of patient data, building upon previous studies in this field. The study critically assesses Fiji's existing healthcare data management system and its challenges. It considers the unique requirements of Fiji's healthcare landscape and endeavors to develop and propose a blockchain-based system, accompanied by recommendations for its implementation. In conclusion, this research provides a brief summary of its key findings and delves into the broader implications for patient data security and healthcare in Fiji. Furthermore, it suggests future avenues for research in this dynamic and evolving field. In an era where reliance on digital health data is growing, blockchain technology emerges as a promising solution for safeguarding patient information in Fiji, laying the groundwork for continued exploration of healthcare information security.

articleTitle: A Game-Theoretic Approach to the Early Detection of Internet of Things-Based Threats in Smart Home Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: In the recent past, there has been rapid development in the Internet of Things (loT) technologies and related applications. As a new paradigm for connecting device machines, loT intends to incorporate the physical world more directly into digital processes. However, with such an innovative technology comes security threats that compromise the system's availability. The study proposed an early detection of loT -based security threats in smart home automation using a game theoretical approach. To assist with early detection, both pure and mixed game theory approaches were employed in an effort to compare how well each one performed with regards to response time. The algorithms and the experimental setup were developed in order to achieve our objective. The results of comparing the early detection of threats to security in loT using pure and mixed game theory strategies have showed that the system performs better with pure game theory than with mixed game theory. The comparison was conducted utilizing alternative evaluated methodologies that employed various strategies. The adoption of a game theoretical approach has demonstrated its efficacy in addressing timely detection challenges in broad system security environments.

articleTitle: Salp Swarm Algorithm Based Optimal Network Reconfiguration with Distributed Generation for Power Loss Minimization and Voltage Profile Improvement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: In a distribution system, power loss and voltage deviation are the main concern for the customers and utility. The distribution system has a lower voltage level and higher amount of flowing current than the transmission system, so that, the percentage real power loss in the distribution system is higher. This study addresses power loss and voltage deviation concerns in distribution systems. It optimizes the Yirgalem-Ethiopia radial distribution network using the Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) and solar Distributed Generation (DG). SSA outperforms other algorithms in reducing real and reactive power losses and improving the voltage profile. The approach minimizes network costs and maintains voltage within acceptable limits. It proves cost-effective, demonstrating significant power loss reduction and improved voltage profiles. The resource feasibility of solar and wind power in Yirgalem city was analyzed and the outcomes showed that solar power generation is more desirable. For this reason, the solar-type Distributed Generation (DG) is used. The proposed SSA algorithm was compared with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) in three various scenarios (only optimal network reconfiguration, only optimal DG size and site, and simultaneous optimal network reconfiguration and DG allocation) for the Aposto feeder. As stated, the SSA method performs better in terms of reducing both real and reactive power losses and improvement of voltage profile. The model has been formulated to minimize the total cost of the network by determining the optima of the substation locations and power, the load transfers between the demand centers, the feeder routes and the load flow in the network subject to a set of constraints. From the point of view of economic evaluations, the proposed approach is cost-effective. Generally, the simulation results show that the proposed technique is effective to maintain all buses voltage magnitude within the IEEE acceptable limit and to reduce power losses significantly.

articleTitle: Development of Gas Insulated Substation in Smart City: Very Fast Raising Overvoltages and its Impacts on Surge Arresters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The development of gas-insulated substations (GIS) in smart cities has ushered in a host of benefits over Air insulated Substation, including compact design, enhanced reliability and resilience, seamless integration of renewable energy sources, and the capability for remote monitoring and control. However, it also presents unique challenges, prominently among them being the generation of very fast raising overvoltages (VFTOs), which can significantly impact the safeguarding of the power system through surge arresters. VFTOs are rapid, high-frequency transient voltage surges that manifest during various switching operations within GIS substations, often linked to disconnector switching, circuit breaker operations, and fault clearance. Surge arresters, also known as lightning arresters or surge protectors, play a pivotal role in GIS substations. They are tasked with protecting vital equipment from voltage surges by skillfully managing residual voltage while suppressing surges originating from GIS operations. The effectiveness of surge arresters in achieving holistic protection hinges on their ability to manage the residual voltages during these very fast rising transients. Interestingly, existing standards from the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) and previous type test reports have traditionally suggested that an increase in the steepness of current surges directly leads to a corresponding increase in residual voltages. However, this work challenges this conventional wisdom and offers contrasting findings. It presents evidence that, particularly during the onset of very fast transient overvoltages (VFTO), the steepness of the surge no longer predominantly influences the residual voltage. These insights are substantiated through extensive simulation exercises carried out using a modified IEEE arrester model on the EMTP-RV platform, benchmarking against existing surge arresters and varying current wave shapes encompassing low, moderate, and higher magnitudes. This groundbreaking discovery has the potential to reshape the approach taken by surge arrester manufacturers. It suggests the need for specialized surge arrester designs that can deliver comprehensive protection against overvoltages originating from GIS substations-an imperative consideration for the ongoing development of smart cities.

articleTitle: Challenges and Opportunities of the Naval Electric Mobility Matrix in the Amazon
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This study addresses the need to improve efficiency in energy conversion and waste management, considering the growing demand for a cleaner and more sustainable energy system. The objective of the research is to map projects and initiatives related to waste management in the Brazilian photovoltaic sector, with an emphasis on the recycling process of photovoltaic (PV) modules. The research included two analyses, an interactive one with interested parties and a second analysis of recycling processes with a case study in the industry. The results showed that recycling PV modules is effective in reducing waste. However, it revealed a lack of consumer knowledge regarding the disposal of these appropriate modules. The study also highlights the importance of reverse logistics in Brazil, especially in the photovoltaic industry, to ensure efficiency and sustainability throughout the life cycle of these materials, making PV energy a clean and sustainable option in the energy transition.

articleTitle: Object Detection and Classification for Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) Through Near-Infrared Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This study proposes a novel pipeline that starts with NIR video data to advance the field of near-infrared (NIR) object detection. NIR video sequences must be split into individual frames to analyze the environment accurately. These frames are then produced and structured for the cutting-edge object identification model YOLOv8. The formatted NIR frames are then used to train the YOLOv8 model, enabling reliable and effective object recognition in complicated maritime settings. Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and autonomous maritime systems have a wide range of potential applications, and the integration of NIR video data and YOLOv8 promises improved object detection capabilities, particularly in low-light and challenging settings. Combining NIR imagery, frame conversion, and YOLOv8 training can dramatically enhance USVs' navigational capabilities and make them more effective in maritime conditions. This study aims to increase autonomy and safety in maritime applications, from surveillance and environmental monitoring to logistics and search and rescue operations.

articleTitle: Hydrogen Horizons: Navigating Challenges and Opportunities for a Sustainable Energy Future
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: The escalating hydrogen demand, expected to surge eightfold by 2050 compared to 2020, poses multifaceted challenges for its energy sector deployment. Hydrogen's exceptional calorific value, ranking second at 120–142 MJ/kg, positions it as the prime energy-to-weight ratio among conventional fuels. Green hydrogen production, with readiness levels around 7–8 and commercial readiness indices of about 4–5, commands a significant 30% market share with 55-80% efficiency and production costs of $4-7/kg H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. While costs are projected to reach $1-2/kg H2 in the future, integrating various production processes is crucial, transcending mass-scale production. Metal hydride emerges as an economical hydrogen storage solution at $125/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, while ammonia leads with a low specific energy cost of $13/GJ. Streamlined infrastructure development is imperative for efficient storage, transportation, and delivery. This exhaustive review encompasses hydrogen production, storage, costs, and applications, offering insightful analysis and guidance on hydrogen's energy carrier challenges. Achieving sustainable development goals by 2050 necessitates integrated planning, infrastructure, cost reduction, net-zero emissions, and innovative storage. Policymakers, researchers, and scientists can utilize this review as a blueprint to shape hydrogen's future role in energy.

articleTitle: Robust Method for Estimating Single-Diode Model Parameters of a PV Module from the Manufacturer's Datasheet Information
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Estimating the electrical model parameters of photovoltaic (PV) modules, which are normally not provided by manufacturers, is crucial for modeling PV systems in simulation studies. This work proposes a novel robust approach to identify parameters of the single diode model (SDM) of a PV module. The equivalent electrical circuit parameters are extracted by solving a set of equations through the application of the Lambert W function for a given value of ideality factor, Ai, based on data found in manufacturer's datasheets under standard test conditions (STC). To find the optimal ideality factor, parameters are computed for different Ai values within a defined range, and their fitness is assessed using a multi-criteria objective function. Irradiance and temperature dependence of the parameters are estimated using the temperature coefficients available on datasheets and the irradiation coefficient of open circuit voltages, calculated using the data at Normal Operating Cell Temperature (NOCT). By utilizing the estimated values for the parameters, the current-voltage (1- V) characteristics at different levels of irradiation and temperatures, and the temperature coefficient of maximum power for several PV modules, were obtained. The errors expressed in terms of root means square deviations compared to the datasheet values were less than 4 % for the five different PV modules considered.

articleTitle: Assessing the Effects of Low Load on Under-Frequency Load Shedding Schemes and Exploring Potential Solutions: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Grid frequency decline under load-generation imbalance can be corrected by shedding a certain amount of load. However, due to the rapid uptake of distributed photovoltaic generation, the visible loads to system operators in distribution feeders are reducing. Traditional load-shedding schemes are facing challenges due to the low-load situation. The required amount of demand reduction cannot be achieved with the traditional load-shedding schemes as before. In some situations, with reverse power flows, load shedding can further increase the generation deficit. Power system operators have temporarily included important loads into UFLS schemes to attain the necessary load levels, but this has reduced the reliability of critical loads. This paper discusses the impacts of the low-load problem and reviews the solutions suggested in the literature.

articleTitle: Electrical Network Optimization Based Vibration Control for Passive Vehicle Cabin
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: During the operation of a vehicle, ground-induced vibrations can lead to an uncomfortable experience for its occupants. To better improve the ride comfort of the commercial vehicle, this paper aims to conduct a further study on the construction and application of the passive cabin suspension layer and the electrical interconnection. A 4-port electrical network (EN) was established in the SIMULINK environment, while concurrently constructing the full-car suspension system model. The EN is embedded into the cabin suspension layer to enable comprehensive interconnection. Theoretically, this pattern of interconnection can isolate cabin motion in three dimensions-heave, pitch, and roll, while the ride comfort and handling stability can be enhanced through adjustment of the circuit components' parameters. Based on the current achievements of the cabin EIS system, this paper creates a constant-velocity road excitation simulation model using the ISO 8608 Class A road profile and cosine speed bumps within the time domain modeling stage. The objective is to assess how driving quality for light commercial vehicles is affected during uneven urban traffic conditions. The particle swarm algorithm in the MATLAB library is used to modify the resistor parameters within the EIS system for different vehicle velocities across varied driving scenarios. The simulation results show that the optimized passive cabin EIS system effectively suppresses the rebound response of the vehicle after sudden bumps.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Product Life Span and Total Lifetime Sales
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Predicting and managing a product's life cycle is essential for enhancing a company's competitiveness. Accurate prediction of a product's total sales volume over its lifespan enables companies to make informed decisions about product planning and sales strategies, leading to improved effectiveness. The objective of this study is to develop a precise hybrid machine-learning model for predicting the total sales volume of a product. To achieve our goal, we propose a hybrid model that combines LGBM (Light Gradient-Boosting Machine) and QBoost (Quantile Boost). LGBM is employed to predict the lifespan of the product, while QBoost utilizes a dataset that includes product lifespan information to predict the total demand over the product's entire lifetime. We assess the performance of our proposed model using four evaluation metrics: RMSE, NRMSE, MAE, and mMAPE. We conduct a comparative analysis of our hybrid model with single models, including Random Forest, LGBM, and QBoost. Additionally, we evaluate the performance of another hybrid model that combines these individual models. The analysis unequivocally demonstrates that the proposed model surpasses benchmark models across all evaluation metrics. This study has significant implications for improving decision-making in product lifecycle management through accurate prediction of product life expectancy and total lifetime sales volume.

articleTitle: Metadata Based Cross-Domain Recommender Framework Using Neighborhood Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: With the overwhelming growth of data there comes a challenge of extracting meaningful and useful information from that data and use it in the most optimized fashion. Modern Recommender Systems (RS) utilize the pattern of user's interest to manage recommendations. However, cold-start users are a daunting challenge in the design of recommender systems since the conventional recommendation services are based on solely one data source. During the recent years, the cross-domain recommendation methods have gained popularity because of the availability of information in multiple domains for cold- start users. The proposed framework, “Metadata based Cross- Domain Recommender Framework using Neighborhood Mapping”(MCDNM) supplements this information by utilizing the data contained in the metadata related to users. This source of information has been mostly ignored by current recommender systems. The rich semantics of metadata are exploited to ex-tract nature of interests of users. The combined advantages of metadata-based and cross-domain approaches are expected to alleviate the issues of cold-start users by transferring user preferences from an auxiliary domain to a target domain. The results demonstrate that the model outperforms the state of the art cross domain recommender systems.

articleTitle: Characterisation of Pyrolysis Oil Produced from Seaweed and Plastic Wastes for Engine Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This research evaluates the potential of pyrolysis oils derived from plastic wastes and seaweed (specifically waste high-density polythene, HDPE) for engine applications. Utilizing a thermal pyrolysis process within a batch reactor, seaweed and HDPE were converted into oil, following preliminary thermogravimetric and CHNS assessments. Experimental conditions varied with temperatures between 400°C to 550°C, maintaining a 60-minutes residence time and a 2-mm feedstock particle size. Results indicated optimal oil yields at 475°C for seaweed (42.93%) and 525°C for HDPE (61.29%). Analytical techniques, including Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), revealed that while seaweed oils were rich in oxygenated compounds, aromatic, phenolic, HDPE oils predominantly contained aromatics and hydrocarbons. Given the higher viscosity (12.01 Cst), density 1.19 (g/cc), and reduced calorific value 29.11(MJ/kg) of seaweed-derived oils compared to HDPE oils (1.63 Cst, 0.78 (g/cc) and 42.89 (MJ/kg respectively) respectively the former might necessitate further refinement for engine compatibility. Conversely, HDPE-derived oil, aligning well with many engine fuel parameters, requires real-world engine testing to validate its potential.

articleTitle: An Analysis Using Reverse Logistics of the Final Life Cycle of Photovoltaic Modules in Brazil
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: This study addresses the need to improve efficiency in energy conversion and waste management, considering the growing demand for a cleaner and more sustainable energy system. The objective of the research is to map projects and initiatives related to waste management in the Brazilian pho-tovoltaic sector, with an emphasis on the recycling process of photovoltaic (PV) modules. The research included two analyses, an interactive one with interested parties and a second analysis of recycling processes with a case study in the industry. The results showed that recycling PV modules is effective in reducing waste. However, it revealed a lack of consumer knowledge regarding the disposal of these appropriate modules. The study also highlights the importance of reverse logistics in Brazil, especially in the photovoltaic industry, to ensure efficiency and sustainability throughout the life cycle of these materials, making PV energy a clean and sustainable option in the energy transition.

articleTitle: CFD Analysis of a Concentrating Solar Thermal Technology in a PCM-Based Storage System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Technology and Engineering (i-COSTE)
abstract: Greenhouse gas emissions (GHE) are increasing due to the use of non-renewable energy sources. These harmful emissions induce us to decide on renewable sources to produce energy. Most of the recent articles suggested that renewable sources are an alternative to producing electrical energy in comparison with non-renewable sources as these will reduce harmful emissions. In this paper, various storage systems and materials were selected to find out the most suitable materials for TES and HTF based on their physical and chemical properties. PCM -based storage systems were selected although many storage systems are available as they absorb and release heat quickly. ANSYS, i.e., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) code “Fluent” was chosen for the simulation of a concentrating solar power (CSP) system with different PCM and HTF materials. The simulation result predicts the performance of different PCM and HTF materials inside the system geometry, thus the efficiency of the system was predicted. Consequently, an improved design could be achieved by evaluating simulation data to obtain better efficiency.
